## Proof

**Claim.** Yes, there exists a finite set of points in which every point has exactly 100 other points at distance 1 from it.

**Construction.** Work in $\mathbb{R}^{100}$ and take the vertex set of the unit hypercube:
$$S \;=\; \{0,1\}^{100} \;\subset\; \mathbb{R}^{100}.$$
This is a finite set with $|S| = 2^{100}$ points.

**Verification.** Take any two points $x = (x_1,\dots,x_{100})$ and $y = (y_1,\dots,y_{100})$ in $S$. Each coordinate satisfies $x_i, y_i \in \{0,1\}$, so each difference $x_i - y_i$ is either $0$ or $\pm 1$. Hence
$$\|x - y\|^2 \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{100}(x_i - y_i)^2 \;=\; k,$$
where $k$ is the number of coordinates in which $x$ and $y$ differ (the Hamming distance). Therefore
$$\|x - y\| = 1 \;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\; k = 1,$$
i.e., $x$ and $y$ are at distance 1 exactly when they differ in precisely one coordinate.

Now fix any point $x \in S$. The points at distance 1 from $x$ are exactly those obtained by flipping a single one of the 100 coordinates of $x$. There are exactly $\binom{100}{1} = 100$ such points, and they are all distinct and all belong to $S$.

Thus every point of $S$ has exactly 100 points of $S$ at distance 1 from it. Since $S$ is finite, this gives the desired example. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE
